subtype: Approach: keeping a simple contact log [Action]
passage: Santosh opened a plain spreadsheet in his Delhi flat and made five columns: name, date, what we talked about, what I promised, follow-up date. He typed in his first row from last week's call with Chandrika, a product manager: 12 March, hiring for the data team, sent her an article, follow up after Diwali. Four more rows followed from his notes. Every Sunday he opened the sheet, wrote thank-you messages to the week's contacts, and set reminders. Two months later, when Chandrika mentioned an opening, he wrote back, "Since we talked in March about the data team, I remembered you were looking for interns." It read like a friend, not a stranger, and it was true because the sheet had kept it.

qa.q: Which five items did Santosh put in the columns?
qa.a: He used name, date, what we talked about, what I promised, and follow-up date.

qa.q: What is Santosh probably feeling when he opens the sheet on Sundays?
qa.a: Santosh is probably calm and quietly hopeful, since he is turning scattered conversations into follow-ups that might lead somewhere.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Santosh add, and why?
qa.a: Santosh could occasionally share something useful without waiting for a reason, because a log keeps track of contacts but goodwill grows from small gifts too.

qa.q: How might Chandrika see the message about the opening?
qa.a: Chandrika receives a note that recalls their March talk and her own interest in interns, so it feels personal and not like a mass message.

grounding: Shows keeping a simple record of each conversation with follow-up dates and thanking people afterwards so that single chats become lasting contacts.

subtype: Approach: keeping a simple contact log [Action]
passage:
'Ramesh, what's that on your laptop? Another sheet?'
'My contact log. Look.' He turned it toward Ayesha. 'Name, date, what we talked about, when to follow up.'
'You met, like, six people at the careers fair.'
'Seven. See: Ms Pillai, 12 March, water-treatment internships, follow up 12 April. Mr Dsouza, 12 March, his team's new plant, follow up after his leave ends.'
'And this column?'
'Thank-you sent. I write to each one the same evening. One line on something they said.'
'Isn't that a lot?'
'Five minutes each. Last year I met great people at fairs and forgot half their names by the next week.' He tapped a row. 'Ms Pillai replied to my thank-you. When I followed up in April, she remembered me and sent the internship form.'
Ayesha pulled out her phone. 'Make me a copy of the sheet?'

qa.q: Which four things does Ramesh note in the log?
qa.a: Name, date, what we talked about, when to follow up.

qa.q: How does Ramesh seem to feel about last year's careers fairs, and what changed?
qa.a: He seems a bit regretful that he forgot half their names, and now feels organised and confident with the log.

qa.q: What else could Ayesha add to her copy of the sheet?
qa.a: A short note on how each person could be helped in return, so the contacts stay two-way and not only requests.

qa.q: How might Ms Pillai see Ramesh's thank-you and later follow-up?
qa.a: She remembers him because of the thank-you, so the follow-up feels like a continuing conversation, and she sends the internship form.

grounding: Shows a student logging name, date, topic and follow-up date for each contact and thanking each person the same day, which turns one meeting into a lasting contact.

subtype: Approach: keeping a simple contact log [Action]
passage:
Back in my second year in Aizawl, I met plenty of interesting people and kept almost none of them. I'm Lalremsiami, and I used to trust my memory. It failed me every time.
So last year I started a plain sheet: name, date, what we talked about, and a date to follow up. After every chat I also sent a thank-you the same day, mentioning one thing I'd learned.
In August I talked to Rekha, a wildlife photographer, for twenty minutes at a book fair. That night I logged her and sent a thank-you about her tip on morning light. The sheet told me to follow up in October. In October I sent her two of my photos taken at dawn, using her tip. She replied with comments, and in December she asked if I'd assist her on a shoot in Dampa.
Twenty minutes at a book fair became my first real work.

qa.a: At a book fair, for twenty minutes.

qa.q: How does Lalremsiami seem to feel looking back at the second year?
qa.a: Lalremsiami seems a bit regretful about losing touch with interesting people and relieved that the sheet now does the remembering.

qa.q: What else could Lalremsiami do to keep the connection with Rekha strong?
qa.a: After the shoot, log it, send a thank-you with one thing learned, and set the next follow-up date.

qa.q: How might Rekha have felt receiving the dawn photos in October?
qa.a: Rekha was likely pleased and flattered to see her tip used, which made her want to offer more help.

grounding: Shows a student logging each contact with a follow-up date and sending same-day thanks, which turns a short chat into lasting work.
